newsitem.title: CANADA: Sask Pool asks Canada to review rail rate.
newsitem.headline: Sask Pool asks Canada to review rail rate.

text.p: Canada's largest grain handler filed an appeal Monday with Canada's Governor in Council to review a decision that cut a rail rate discount.

"According to the Canadian Transportation Agency's assessment, the risk associated with moving grain is the same as the risk associated with other bulk commodities. As a result, the CTA removed a one percent downward adjustment that has been applied to the cost of capital," Saskatchewan Wheat Pool president Leroy Larsen said in a statement.
Cutting the cost of capital discount raises maximum freight rate scale for grain to C$0.40 a tonne from C$0.30, Larsen said.
The total grain and oilseed freight rate bill would rise by an additional C$10 to C$12 million a year, he added.
"The decision ignores the fact that the railways have not shared the benefits of increased productivity since 1992," Larsen said.
Canadian National Railway Co and CP Rail System cut staff and shed track since 1992.
